name: Hanan
overview: Hanan was a male Levite known for his role in distributing portions to his kinsmen, as recorded in Nehemiah 13:13. His service reflects the responsibilities entrusted to Levites in maintaining the welfare and order of their community. No additional personal notes are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Hanan means 'gracious' in Hebrew. This proper name, as noted in Nehemiah 13:13, does not appear to have been given directly by God but reflects a common Hebrew name of the period.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Hanan as the son of Zaccur, as explicitly stated in Nehemiah 13:13. Beyond this father-son relationship, no other family connections are recorded for him.
scriptureSignificance: Hanan's significance lies in his service as a Levite who distributed portions to the community, highlighting the practical duties of the Levites in supporting their fellow tribesmen. His mention in Nehemiah 13:13 situates him within the post-exilic restoration period, emphasizing the restoration of proper worship and community order under God's guidance.
